purpose: Data points for the readiness rubric: one entry per rubric-judge dispatch, the prompt as sent, what the judge loaded, its model tier, and what it found.
prompt_template:
Judge the draft against the rubric and return the verdict sheet as your reply.

Inputs:
- draft: <project root>/dev/workspace/runs/agent-spec-interviewer/spec.v1.json
- nine-domains description: <project root>/dev/workspace/filebox/spec/spec-description.md
- verification addendum (product is agent-shaped): <project root>/dev/workspace/filebox/spec/spec-description-verification-addendum.md
- rubric: <project root>/dev/workspace/filebox/spec/spec-readiness-rubric.md

Every answer quotes its evidence from the draft.

findings.text: intent names an activity, not an outcome condition
B1 and B21 each carry two decisions
byte-identical condition orphaned at the gate
acceptance boundary includes a schema SC9 excludes

advisory: QINT.3 mechanism in intent (rejected: provider keeps it)

runs.prompt: prompt_template plus: 'Write the full verdict sheet to <run folder>/judge/verdict-v1-run3.md and return the same sheet as your reply.' (judge reported it has no Write tool and returned text only; sheet persisted by the builder)
runs.draft_state: 23 behaviours, 17 edges, 13 constraints; I8 reuse pointer corrected before dispatch

findings.text: 'Model tier: small|standard|inherit' in I6/I7/I8 is run conduct
findings.disposition: absorbed by deletion, then reopened by provider as P-dispatch-tier; closed: tier lives in the dispatched agent's frontmatter, I6-I8 'dispatched by name; no model parameter', D7

findings.text: B6 bundles node creation, problem state, no re-confirmation
probe transcript appears first in ACC, not VER
findings.disposition: absorbed: VER probe sentence, ACC records/probe.txt

advisory: QDOD.3 'has been read' is an activity (fixed alongside QDOD.1)

findings.text: C2 'exits 0 before any rubric-judge dispatch' is a step; duplicates B10
findings.disposition: absorbed: C2 restated as a condition on the draft a verdict sheet names

findings.text: B16 chains explorer wave then re-ask
findings.disposition: absorbed: B16 split into B16, B25; D18; VER

advisory: QGEN.3 C6/B19 restate the write boundary

findings.text: B3 bundles draft timing and draft completeness
findings.disposition: absorbed: B3 split into B3, B26; E17; VER

findings.text: ACC path boundary lies outside C6, which SC12 named as the edit limit; SC12 contradicts SC1
findings.disposition: absorbed: SC12 reworded to the DoD's path list

advisory: QGEN.3 C4/B20 restate the read boundary

runs.experiment: rubric + draft only; standard and addendum withheld
runs.prompt:
Judge the draft against the rubric and return the verdict sheet as your reply.

Inputs:
- draft: <project root>/dev/workspace/runs/agent-spec-interviewer/spec.v1.json
- rubric: <project root>/dev/workspace/filebox/spec/spec-readiness-rubric.md

Open only these two files. Every answer quotes its evidence from the draft.
runs.draft_state: 26 behaviours, 17 edges, 14 constraints (run-5 findings absorbed before dispatch, so not a clean A/B against run 5)
advisory: QINT.3 mechanism in intent (same as every run)
QGEN.3 yes: C/B pairs not flagged without the standard
judge disclosed the withheld inputs in its header rather than absorbing the deviation
runs.gate_status: not used as the gate; the standard dispatch carries four inputs, so a four-input run is still owed before the attacker

observations: QBEH.2 fired on four of four completed runs, each time on a different behaviour, because the sample changes as behaviours are split and word counts shift; the rubric never sees the whole set.
Sampling by 'three longest' tends to pick the successors of the previous run's splits (B24, B25), so each split feeds the next sample.
QINT.3 (advisory) has fired identically on every run since the provider decided to keep the mechanism in the intent; the rubric has no way to record a rejected advisory.
QGEN.3 (advisory) flags constraint/behaviour pairs (C4/B20, C6/B19) that the check-claiming rule requires: a constraint and the behaviour that makes it checkable across a session.
Each sonnet run took roughly five to six minutes and about 38k tokens with four files loaded.
Run 3's request to write the sheet to a file was declined by the judge (no Write tool); the builder persists sheets.

Run 6 (rubric + draft only) passed every block including QGEN.3 and QBEH.2; runs 3-5 with the standard and addendum loaded failed QBEH.2 every time. Confounded by the draft having changed between runs, but QBEH.2's run-6 reasoning ('disjunctive outcome phrasing describes one exhaustive result-state, not two decisions') is a reading the standard-loaded judges never took.
Without the standard, the judge did not flag C/B pairs under QGEN.3; that finding came from the standard's placement rules, not the rubric's question.
Run 6 cost 205s and 31k tokens against 300-356s and ~38k for four-input runs: about 20% cheaper.
The judge disclosed the missing inputs in its header unprompted, so a judge given fewer files than its rubric names will say so rather than guess.
